First, a quick recap:

Putt posted a comment earlier today that explained the main reasons he's been quiet or seemingly inactive. Basically, time constraints, inability to satisfy everyone, and exhaustion. Mostly things I've written of here before.

Then Putt posted the first announcement since December of last year, in which he reiterated the ideas within the above comment, but also explained the cause of the recent Voat downtime (the "webserver ran out of disk space on the primary drive").

So the announcement came, the canary was updated, the downtime was due to a technical error, Putt's just been low on time and energy these last few months, and his "disappearance" was in fact akin to a vacation.

At the same time, in the announcement Putt said that after reflection he understands the concerns people had, and even apologized for not being super communicative and for being snappy with some oldgoats (even though I think the latter was perfectly justified).

So what lessons have been learned? Well, for one I think the userbase could afford to be a little (or a lot) more understanding in the future of Putt's position, and less prone to jumping to exciting conclusions. Putt's been with Voat for a long time, and he's been reliable for a long time. Maybe not hyper-efficient, but can we really expect that level of efficiency given his position? Given his reliability, perhaps, for our own sakes, we can be somewhat more trusting and patient in the future.

On the other side of things, everyone seems to agree communication could use some kind of work. If anything has been made glaringly clear these past weeks, it's the fact that the users here actually care quite a bit about Putt. Many were even able to reluctantly accept the possibility of Voat's demise, but no one wanted to accept that Putt might have been hurt. Having a semi-reliable way of knowing Putt is at the very least alive and free would alleviate the fears of even the most patient among us. As for the impatient, it may not be possible to alleviate their concerns.
